message.content:
You are reverse-engineering a compiled C++ binary as a BLACK BOX. The binary is at /workspace/dataset/test15_executable.

Invocation contract: it takes EXACTLY 6 positional args: scheme host port path query fragment.
It prints 8 lines to stdout: scheme(), host(), port(), path(), query(), fragment(), to_string(), is_valid().

RULES OF ENGAGEMENT:
- You may ONLY run the binary and observe stdout/stderr/exit code. There is NO C++ source available; do not look for any.
- ALWAYS quote every argument in the shell, including empty ones: /workspace/dataset/test15_executable "http" "example.com" "80" "/" "" ""
- Make output unambiguous. Use a helper that numbers the lines and marks empties, e.g.:
    p(){ printf '### IN: [%s]\n' "$*"; /workspace/dataset/test15_executable "$@" >/tmp/o 2>/tmp/e; printf '  exit=%d\n' $?; nl -ba -s': ' /tmp/o | sed 's/$/<END>/'; if [ -s /tmp/e ]; then echo "  STDERR: $(cat /tmp/e)"; fi; }
  Then call p with 6 quoted args. Beware: trailing empty args are easy to lose — verify your helper really passes 6.
- Run MANY cases (30+ minimum). Batch them into a few Bash calls; do not do one call per case.
- Be exhaustive about the boundary cases in your assigned dimension.
- Do not guess. Every rule you report must be backed by an observed input/output pair you actually ran.

Baseline facts already established (re-verify if relevant to you):
- ("http","example.com","80","/","","")  -> lines: http / example.com / 80 / "/" / "" / "" / "http://example.com:80/" / 1
- ("http","example.com","-1","/","","") -> to_string is "http://example.com/"  (port omitted), port() prints -1
- ("http","example.com","0","/","","")  -> to_string is "http://example.com:0/"  (port 0 IS included)
- ("http","","80","/","","")            -> to_string is "http://:80/", is_valid=1
- ("","example.com","80","/","","")     -> to_string is "/" (scheme+authority both vanish), is_valid=1
- ("","","0","","","")                  -> to_string is "", is_valid=0

Report rules as precise, implementable statements (pseudocode-level), each with the concrete evidence line.


DIMENSION: what from_components does to the host string before storing it (line 2 = host()).

- Case: "EXAMPLE.COM", "Example.Com" -> lowercased?
- Whitespace: " example.com", "example.com ", "exa mple.com", tab/newline embedded.
- Trailing dot "example.com.", leading dot, double dots "a..b".
- IPv6 forms: "[::1]", "::1", "[2001:db8::1]".
- With port embedded: "example.com:8080" -> is the colon part split off into port, or kept in host?
- With userinfo embedded: "user:pass@example.com" -> split into userinfo (check whether to_string gains "user:pass@")?
- With a path embedded: "example.com/foo".
- Percent-encoded "%65xample.com" -> decoded?
- Uppercase non-ASCII UTF-8 bytes: "ÉXAMPLE.com" -> any byte mangling?
- Very long host (400 chars).
Report exactly which of these are transformed vs stored verbatim, and how line 7 (to_string) reflects it.

attachment.content:
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

input.dimension: host: what from_components does to the host string before storing it (line 2 = host(), and how line 7 to_string reflects it)

rules.rule: host is stored 100% VERBATIM: from_components performs NO transformation of any kind on the host argument. host() (line 2) is always byte-for-byte identical to argv[2]. Pseudocode: this->host_ = argv_host; (no copy-transform, no trim, no case fold, no encode/decode, no parse).
rules.evidence:
60+ cases all echo input exactly. Byte-exact proof: ("http","example.com","80","/","","") -> stdout hex ` 68 74 74 70 0a 65 78 61 0d 6d 70 6c 65 2e 63 6f 6d 0a 38 30 0a 2f 0a 0a 0a 68 74 74 70 3a 2f 2f 65 78 61 0d 6d 70 6c 65 2e 63 6f 6d 3a 38 30 2f 0a 31 0a` which is byte-identical (51 bytes) to `printf 'http
example.com
80
/


http://example.com:80/
1
'`

rules.rule: NO lowercasing / no case folding of host. Uppercase and mixed case are preserved in both host() and to_string(). This is NOT because the program lacks a lowercase step — scheme IS lowercased in the very same run, so host is deliberately/accidentally exempt.
rules.evidence: ("HTTP","EXAMPLE.COM","443","/","","") -> line1: `http` (scheme LOWERCASED), line2: `EXAMPLE.COM` (host NOT lowercased), line7: `http://EXAMPLE.COM:443/`. Also ("http","Example.Com",...) -> line2 `Example.Com`, line7 `http://Example.Com:80/`; ("http","eXaMpLe.CoM",...) -> line2 `eXaMpLe.CoM`

rules.rule: Case behavior is locale-independent: setting LC_ALL does not introduce host folding.
rules.evidence: LC_ALL=C, LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8 and LC_ALL=tr_TR.UTF-8 with ("HTTP","EXAMPLE.COM","80","/","","") all produce identical output: line1 `http`, line2 `EXAMPLE.COM`, line7 `http://EXAMPLE.COM:80/`

rules.rule: NO whitespace trimming at all — leading, trailing, and interior spaces are kept, and they are emitted raw into to_string (producing a URL with literal spaces).
rules.evidence: ("http"," example.com","80","/","","") -> line2 `[space]example.com`, line7 `http:// example.com:80/`; ("http","example.com ",...) -> line7 `http://example.com :80/`; ("http","  example.com  ",...) -> line7 `http://  example.com  :80/`; ("http","exa mple.com",...) -> line7 `http://exa mple.com:80/`; ("http"," ",...) -> line2 ` `, line7 `http:// :80/`

rules.rule: Control characters (TAB 0x09, CR 0x0d, LF 0x0a, 0x01, 0x02, 0x7f) are stored verbatim in host and re-emitted verbatim in to_string. An embedded LF makes the 8-line output visually become 10 lines because host() and to_string() each print the raw newline.
rules.evidence: TAB: expected-vs-actual hex identical `...65 78 61 09 6d 70 6c 65...`. LF: hex `68 74 74 70 0a 65 78 61 0a 6d 70 6c 65 2e 63 6f 6d 0a 38 30 ...` (51 bytes, matches verbatim expectation); numbered output showed lines `2: exa`, `3: mple.com`, `8: http://exa`, `9: mple.com:80/`, `10: 1`. Ctrl bytes: ("http","a\x01\x02b.com",...) -> od `61 01 02 62 2e 63 6f 6d` in both line2 and line7

rules.rule: NO dot normalization: trailing dot, leading dot, doubled dots, and bare "."/".." are all kept as-is.

NO IPv6 bracket handling: brackets are neither added to a bare IPv6 literal nor stripped from a bracketed one. "[::1]" stays bracketed, "::1" stays unbracketed, and when a port is also present the bare form yields the ambiguous "host:port" concatenation.

NO port splitting: a colon+digits suffix inside host is NOT parsed out into port(). The host keeps the embedded ":8080" and the separate port argument is appended after it, producing a double port in to_string.
rules.evidence: ("http","example.com:8080","80","/","","") -> line2 `example.com:8080`, line3 `80`, line7 `http://example.com:8080:80/`. With port=-1 the appended port is omitted so the embedded one survives alone: ("http","example.com:8080","-1","/","","") -> line7 `http://example.com:8080/`. Also "example.com:" -> `http://example.com::80/`, ":8080" -> `http://:8080:80/`, ":" -> `http://::80/`

rules.rule: NO userinfo extraction: "user:pass@host" is kept whole in host(). There is no separate userinfo field; to_string does not gain a distinct "user:pass@" component — it simply reprints the host string (which happens to contain it).
rules.evidence: ("http","user:pass@example.com","80","/","","") -> line2 `user:pass@example.com`, line7 `http://user:pass@example.com:80/`; ("http","user@example.com",...) -> line2 `user@example.com`; ("http","user:pass@example.com:8080","-1",...) -> line2 `user:pass@example.com:8080`, line7 `http://user:pass@example.com:8080/`; "@@" -> line2 `@@`, line7 `http://@@:80/`

rules.rule: NO path/query/fragment/scheme extraction from host: '/', '?', '#', and even a full "scheme://" prefix embedded in host stay inside host, and to_string blindly appends ":port" + path after them, producing a malformed URL.
rules.evidence: ("http","example.com/foo","80","/","","") -> line2 `example.com/foo`, line4 `/`, line7 `http://example.com/foo:80/`; ("http","example.com?q=1","80","/","","") -> line5 empty, line7 `http://example.com?q=1:80/`; ("http","example.com#frag","80","/","","") -> line6 empty, line7 `http://example.com#frag:80/`; ("http","//example.com",...) -> line7 `http:////example.com:80/`; ("http","http://example.com",...) -> line7 `http://http://example.com:80/`

rules.rule: NO percent-decoding and NO percent-encoding of the host: valid escapes are not decoded, and lone/invalid '%' is not escaped or rejected.
rules.evidence: ("http","%65xample.com","80","/","","") -> line2 `%65xample.com` (not `example.com`), line7 `http://%65xample.com:80/`; "%45XAMPLE.com" -> line2 `%45XAMPLE.com`; "exa%20mple.com" -> line2 `exa%20mple.com`; "%" -> line2 `%`, line7 `http://%:80/`; "%zz" -> line2 `%zz`; "%%41" -> line2 `%%41`

rules.rule: NO byte mangling of non-ASCII / high-bit bytes: UTF-8 multibyte sequences and raw bytes >= 0x80 pass through untouched (no IDNA/punycode, no 8-bit tolower).
rules.evidence: ("http","ÉXAMPLE.com","80","/","","") -> od shows `303 211 X A M P L E . c o m` (0xC3 0x89 preserved, É NOT folded to é) in both line2 and line7 `http://ÉXAMPLE.com:80/`; ("http","a\x7f\xffb",...) -> od `61 177 377 62` in line2 and again in line7; "日本.example" -> line7 `http://日本.example:80/`; "ÄÖÜ.example" -> line2 `ÄÖÜ.example`

rules.rule: NO length limit, truncation, or validation by length. Host is stored and re-emitted in full at every size tested; line7 length == 7 + len(host) + 4 for "http://"+host+":80/".
rules.evidence: lengths 63,64,253,254,255,256,400,1000,2000 all: exit=0, line2 length == input length and string-compares equal to input ("verbatim"), valid=1, empty stderr. e.g. in_len=1000 -> line2_len=1000 verbatim, line7_len=1011; 400-char host -> line7 = `http://aaa...aaa:80/` length 411; a 170-char mixed `A.%41A.%41...` host is also verbatim

rules.rule: host has NO effect on validity as a character class — no host value observed makes is_valid 0. Instead is_valid (line 8) == (host is non-empty) OR (path is non-empty); host merely contributes its non-emptiness, and even a single-space host counts as non-empty.

to_string reflects host by plain concatenation, gated entirely on scheme: if scheme != "" then out += scheme + "://" + host + (port >= 0 ? ":" + to_string(port) : ""). The "//" is emitted even when host is empty.
If scheme is empty, the entire authority — including a non-empty host and the port — is DROPPED from to_string, even though host() still reports it verbatim.

No diagnostics ever: every host value tested returns exit code 0 with zero bytes on stderr and exactly 8 printed values (newline-embedded hosts still print 8 values, just spread over more physical lines).
rules.evidence: All runs printed `exit=0`; `test15_executable http EXAMPLE.COM 80 / '' '' 2>&1 >/dev/null | wc -c` -> 0; stdout line count -> 8; long-host loop reported stderr=0 bytes for every length including 2000

uncertainties: A NUL byte (0x00) cannot be passed through argv, so I could not test whether a host containing an embedded NUL is truncated. All other byte values 0x01-0xFF were tested as verbatim.

I could not distinguish 'host stored verbatim' from 'host stored verbatim after a no-op transformation pass' — the observable behavior is identical. Only the externally visible result (host() and to_string()) is proven verbatim.
Because scheme IS lowercased while host is not, this looks like an intentional asymmetry (or a bug) in from_components, but the binary gives no way to confirm intent.
Hosts above 2000 chars were not tested (2000 worked fine with valid=1 and no truncation); there may be some very large limit driven by allocation, not by URL logic.

is_valid == (!host.empty() || !path.empty()) is consistent with all 10 emptiness-probe cases I ran, but query/fragment/port were only varied in a few combinations, so a more exotic interaction is not fully excluded (this is primarily the validity dimension, not host).

Whether host affects to_string when the scheme is empty but a port is set was tested only with port 80 and -1 (both dropped the authority entirely); other port values were not swept in the empty-scheme case.
